name: QĐ 1705/QĐ-TTg — Chiến lược Giáo dục 2030
issuer: Prime Minister of Vietnam (Thủ tướng Chính phủ)
note: Vietnam's National Education Strategy to 2030, vision 2045; references QĐ 127/QĐ-TTg (AI Strategy 2030); promotes digital transformation and AI in education; no academic integrity provisions for AI — a policy vacuum alongside Decree 109/2022
dinh_nghia: Decision 1705/QĐ-TTg (issued October 2024) is Vietnam's National Education Development Strategy to 2030, with a vision to 2045. It establishes the overarching framework for Vietnamese education reform: shifting from knowledge-transmission to competency-based education (phát triển năng lực), human-centered learning, lifelong learning society, and digital transformation. The strategy explicitly promotes AI integration in education as a tool for improving quality and access but does not define or regulate AI-assisted academic work or academic integrity in AI contexts.
phan_loai: QĐ 1705 operates at a strategic (not regulatory) level. It defines policy direction across: (1) curriculum reform (competency-based); (2) digital transformation and AI in education; (3) teacher development; (4) university autonomy (tự chủ đại học); (5) lifelong learning and disadvantaged group support; (6) international integration. Academic integrity is NOT a categorized policy area — the gap is structural, not incidental.
lich_su_khai_niem: QĐ 1705 supersedes the previous Vietnam Education Strategy 2011-2020. It was developed 2022-2024 as part of Vietnam's implementation of Resolution 29-NQ/TW (2013) on fundamental and comprehensive education reform. The October 2024 timing postdates ChatGPT (Nov 2022) and Decree 109/2022 (eff. March 2023) yet still contains no AI academic integrity provisions — indicating the policy gap is deliberate or overlooked at the highest policy level.
ten_truong_hop: QĐ 1705/QĐ-TTg — Quyết định phê duyệt Chiến lược phát triển giáo dục đến năm 2030, tầm nhìn đến năm 2045. Issued by the Prime Minister, October 2024. Applies to the entire Vietnamese national education system from preschool through university.
dien_bien: The strategy mandates: by 2030, 100% of universities implement digital learning management systems; AI tools integrated into teaching and assessment; teachers receive AI competency training; a national lifelong learning platform. Cross-references QĐ 127/QĐ-TTg (National AI Strategy to 2030) for technical implementation. Human-centered education (lấy con người làm trung tâm) is a core principle — framing learning outcomes around individual student development rather than standardized knowledge delivery. The AI strategy cross-reference (QĐ 127) promotes AI development but does not include academic integrity safeguards.
ket_qua_xu_ly: As a strategy document, QĐ 1705 sets targets and directions rather than enforcement mechanisms. Implementation relies on MOET issuing implementing decrees, circulars, and institutional guidelines. Targets include: 50% of university students having AI literacy by 2028 [uncertain exact figure]; international ranking of Vietnamese universities improving to top 500 QS by 2030 for 5+ universities [uncertain]. Academic integrity outcomes are not specified as targets.
con_so_thong_ke: Strategy timeframe: 2030 primary target, 2045 vision. Budget: state education spending floor at minimum 20% of total state budget. AI references: cross-references QĐ 127/QĐ-TTg (National AI Strategy). University autonomy expansion: targets increasing self-financing capacity. Vietnam's HE enrollment target: 260+ students per 10,000 population by 2030 [uncertain exact figure].
hai_cho_nguoi_hoc: QĐ 1705's competency-based framework requires genuine skill development, which AI fraud directly undermines. If AI is promoted as a tool without academic integrity safeguards, students may use it to produce competency-based assessments without developing the underlying competencies — defeating the strategy's core objective of shifting from knowledge transmission to genuine capability building.
hai_cho_nghien_cuu: The strategy's research quality improvement goals (ranking improvements, increased international publications) could be undermined if AI-assisted fabrication is not addressed. Vietnamese research publications have faced scrutiny for integrity issues; a strategy that promotes AI without integrity safeguards risks exacerbating this.
hai_cho_xa_hoi: The gap between QĐ 1705's stated goal of 'education as the foundation of national development' and the lack of integrity provisions creates a risk of credential inflation on a national scale. If AI fraud rates are as high as Springer 2024 research suggests (3x self-reported rates), the competency-based degrees QĐ 1705 aims to produce may not reflect genuine competencies.
cong_cu_phat_hien: QĐ 1705 does not specify or fund academic integrity detection tools. The digital transformation provisions (LMS adoption, digital assessment) could theoretically enable process-based detection (revision history, timestamp analysis) but no policy framework connects digital infrastructure to academic integrity.
han_che_cong_cu: The strategy's emphasis on AI tool adoption without corresponding integrity frameworks creates an institutional incentive to promote AI use without critically examining misuse. Top-down AI adoption targets could pressure institutions to deprioritize integrity measures that might reduce apparent AI utilization metrics.
watermarking: Not mentioned in QĐ 1705 or its cross-referenced QĐ 127. Vietnam's national AI strategy focuses on AI development, deployment, and digital transformation — not on AI output authentication or watermarking for academic integrity purposes.
thiet_ke_bai_tap: QĐ 1705's competency-based education mandate (phát triển năng lực) implicitly favors authentic, process-based assessment — which aligns with AI-resistant assessment design. However, this connection is not made explicit. The strategy creates policy space for process-based assessment reform but does not direct it toward AI integrity specifically.
chinh_sach_truong_hoc: University autonomy provisions (tự chủ đại học) in QĐ 1705 delegate AI policy to individual institutions, consistent with the Decree 109 framework. This means AI academic integrity policy remains fragmented across 500+ institutions without national minimum standards.
van_hoa_to_chuc: The strategy's human-centered framing (lấy con người làm trung tâm) is philosophically aligned with values-based academic integrity culture (McCabe model). However, without explicit policy direction, this alignment remains rhetorical rather than operational.
ai_literacy: QĐ 1705 explicitly promotes digital literacy and AI competency as part of the education reform agenda, cross-referencing QĐ 127. However, AI literacy in the strategy means competency to USE AI tools productively — not AI literacy in the sense of understanding AI limitations, bias, and ethical use. The distinction between productive AI use and AI-assisted dishonesty is not addressed.
khung_quoc_te: QĐ 1705 positions Vietnam's education goals in relation to ASEAN and global benchmarks (QS rankings, PISA scores, UNESCO SDG 4). UNESCO 2023 GenAI guidance explicitly links digital transformation with academic integrity safeguards — a linkage absent from QĐ 1705. EU AI Act Article 50 and UNESCO recommendations on AI in education (2023) represent international standards that Vietnam's strategy does not yet reflect.
phap_luat_viet_nam: QĐ 1705 and Nghị định 109/2022/NĐ-CP together constitute Vietnam's legal/policy framework for education. Neither addresses AI academic integrity. The combined gap creates a policy vacuum: Decree 109 defines integrity categories (without AI), QĐ 1705 promotes AI adoption (without integrity safeguards) — two policies moving in opposite directions without a bridging provision.
chinh_sach_chau_a: Singapore's national education policy (MOE) explicitly addresses AI integrity alongside AI adoption — a model QĐ 1705 could follow. South Korea and Japan have similar dual-track policies. Vietnam's strategy lags regional peers in integrating integrity safeguards into AI-in-education promotion.
ai_tutor_vs_ai_cheater: QĐ 1705 unambiguously frames AI as 'tutor' — a tool for improving learning quality, teacher development, and educational access. The strategy's silence on the 'AI as cheater' dimension reflects a policy choice (or oversight) to promote adoption without addressing misuse — creating an implicitly permissive environment.
edtech_company_policies: QĐ 1705's digital transformation provisions create market opportunities for EdTech companies in Vietnam (LMS providers, AI tutoring platforms, digital assessment tools). FPT Education and Coursera partnerships align with the strategy's goals. Without integrity requirements in the strategy, EdTech companies face no mandate to build academic integrity features into their Vietnam-market products.
de_xuat_nha_nghien_cuu: As an EdTech researcher: (1) Recommend that MOET issue a supplementary circular to QĐ 1705 explicitly linking AI adoption targets with academic integrity safeguards; (2) Propose that AI literacy (QĐ 1705 target) be defined to include understanding of AI misuse and academic integrity — following UNESCO 2023 guidelines; (3) Advocate for a national pilot program combining QĐ 1705 digital infrastructure with process-based assessment (Google Docs revision history, staged submissions) to establish AI-resistant assessment as a national standard; (4) Request that Vietnam join UNESCO's Global Education Coalition to access international academic integrity in AI frameworks; (5) Use QĐ 1705's 20% education budget floor to fund institutional academic integrity infrastructure including detection tools and faculty training.
bai_bao_khoa_hoc: Nguyen et al. (2024) Springer — AI cheating prevalence among Vietnamese undergraduates, doi:10.1007/s10639-024-12495-4. UNESCO (2023) Guidance for generative AI in education and research. No peer-reviewed analysis of QĐ 1705's AI integrity gap identified in literature as of 2024 [uncertain].
